title: A Traceability Study of the Rice Supply Chain and Related Products
content: Analytical traceability of agri-food products complements documentary systems by verifying consistency between a product and its declared origin. In this study, the relative distribution of lanthanides was evaluated as geochemical fingerprint to trace provenance information along the rice supply chain, considering matrices subjected to different biological and technological transformations. The concentrations of macroelements, microelements, trace and ultra trace elements were determined by ICP-OES and ICP-MS; the lanthanide profiles of the different stages of the supply chain were normalised to cerium (following a procedure already exploited by the authors in traceability studies) and quantitatively compared using the L parameter, calculated as the sum of the relative differences between Ce-normalised lanthanide concentrations. The investigation included different rice varieties, seeds, plant compartments, brown and white rice, other cereal species and a processed product (pasta made from rice). The results showed that, despite the variations in absolute concentrations and fractionations associated with biological and technological processes, the relative structure of the lanthanide fingerprint remained overall recognisable along the supply chain. Overall, the results highlight the potential of the relative distribution of lanthanides as a complementary tool to link soil, crop, and products through geochemical provenance information.
